discovery: The optical lattice clock and quantum-limited optical frequency metrology with neutral atoms

nominees.name: Hidetoshi Katori
nominees.affiliation: University of Tokyo and RIKEN, Japan

nominees.name: Jun Ye
nominees.affiliation: JILA, NIST and University of Colorado Boulder, USA

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / precision measurement
motivation: Katori's insight of the 'magic wavelength' let thousands of neutral atoms be confined in an optical lattice without perturbing the clock transition. It removed the conflict between trapping and accuracy, and gave clocks the stability of many atoms with the precision of a single trapped ion. Katori demonstrated the first lattice clocks. Ye turned the concept into systems of unprecedented stability and accuracy, reaching the 10^-18 level and beyond. He did this through ultrastable lasers, control of interactions in degenerate Fermi gases, and spatially resolved measurements of gravitational redshift at the millimetre scale. The clocks are now adopted worldwide. They are driving the redefinition of the SI second, enabling relativistic geodesy, testing variations of fundamental constants, and giving platforms for entanglement-enhanced metrology. It is a simple, general idea whose impact is shown by how widely it has been used.
